name: Aragonese
catalog_citation: Mott, Brian. 2007. Chistabino (Pyrenean Aragonese). Journal of the International Phonetic Association 37(1): 103-114. doi:10.1017/S0025100306002842
catalog_locator: p. 110 (PDF p. 8 of 12), section 'Prosody' > 'Lexical stress'; file, page image
catalog_quote: Words in Chistabino are usually stressed on the penultimate or final syllable, as in all Aragonese accents: desenfaixa [deseɱˈfai̯ʃa] ‘s/he undoes the bundle of grass’, desenfaixar [deseɱfai̯ˈʃa] ‘to undo a bundle of grass’. Antepenultimate stress is much rarer than in Spanish, though you sometimes find hypercorrect forms like pántano [ˈpan̪tano] ‘reservoir’ (Spanish pantano [pan̪ˈtano]). In third person imperatives, the antepenultimate stress of Spanish is avoided by the fact that the reflexive pronoun precedes the verb: s’asiente usté [saˈsjen̪te usˈte], s’asienten ustés [saˈsjen̪ten usˈtes] ‘sit down’ (cf. Spanish siéntese usted, siéntense ustedes).

new_statements.rule_in_words: Romance-type lexical/morphological stress confined in practice to the last two syllables: penultimate or final depending on the word (e.g. verb form desenfáixa vs infinitive desenfaixár); antepenultimate stress is marginal (rarer than in Spanish, avoided/regularised to penultimate), so stress is not predictable from a single fixed position but falls within a final two-(three-)syllable window. Corroborated by EFA 2017 Gramatica Basica sec. 1.2.1.1 (agudas/planas/esdruixolas; 'l'aragonés gosa refusar las parolas esdruixolas, tornando-las en planas') and AAL 2023 Ortografía 3.2c/4.3.
new_statements.secondary_stress: Mott says nothing on secondary stress. AAL 2023 Ortografía 3.5c: adverbs in -ment are final-stressed and 'pueden presentar un acento secundario en o lexema' (may carry a secondary accent on the lexical base).
new_statements.exceptions: Antepenultimate stress rare (hypercorrect pántano; toponyms per EFA 2017; habitual in some varieties such as ansotano per AAL 2023 3.2c); learned proparoxytones adapted as paroxytones (grafico, medico). Phrase-final unstressed syllables, especially south of Huesca and in the Ebro Valley, may be lengthened with a pitch rise, giving an impression of stress displacement (less noticeable in Chistabino).
new_statements.domain_note: Word-level lexical stress; Mott separately describes phrase-level prominence (final-syllable lengthening/pitch rise in intonation units) and states the nuclear tone falls on the last stressed syllable of the intonation phrase (p.111). Description is of the Chistabino (Gistaín valley) dialect but the stress statement is explicitly generalised to 'all Aragonese accents'.
new_statements.identity_note: Mott 2007 describes Chistabino, the Aragonese of the Gistaín (Chistau) valley, Huesca (speakers from Gistaín/Serveto); no separate Glottolog code known to me under arag1245 for this variety. The stress sentence is explicitly generalised by the author to 'all Aragonese accents', and the EFA 2017 grammar and AAL 2023 orthography (both for standard/common Aragonese) agree: final or penultimate stress, proparoxytones rare and regularised to penultimate (except e.g. ansotano and toponyms).

sources.note: p.110 'Prosody / Lexical stress': words usually stressed on the penultimate or final syllable, 'as in all Aragonese accents'; antepenultimate stress much rarer than in Spanish (hypercorrect pántano); phrase-final unstressed syllables may get lengthening + pitch rise giving an impression of stress displacement (less so in Chistabino); nuclear tone falls on last stressed syllable of the intonation phrase (p.111).

sources.note: Sec. 1.2.1.1 (printed pp.3-4, PDF pp.41-42): polysyllabic words have one stressed syllable; agudas (final), planas (penultimate), esdruixolas (antepenultimate); proparoxytones 'no son guaire comuns en aragonés, ya que l'aragonés gosa refusar las parolas esdruixolas, tornando-las en planas', though found in toponymy. Sec. 1.4.1 gives written-accent rules.

sources.citation: Academia Aragonesa de la Lengua. 2023. Ortografía de l'aragonés. Zaragoza. 29 pp.
sources.note: Ch.3 (PDF p.13): accent-mark rules by agudas/planas/esdruixulas; where pronunciation vacillates between plana and esdruixula the plana form is recommended 'seguindo la tendencia prosodica de l'aragonés moderno: grafico, medico', but in varieties like ansotano proparoxytone pronunciation is habitual; adverbs in -ment are agudas with a possible secondary accent on the lexeme (3.5c). Sec. 4.3 (PDF p.15): Greek/Latin proparoxytone cultismos are adapted as paroxytones in modern Aragonese.
